# RangerFlow vs React Flow — performance

**Generated by `npm run rangerflow:bench:compare`.** Node v22.14.0, this machine.

What is compared in Node is the shared *math*: edge-path generation
(`@xyflow/system` vs `EdgeRouter`) and force layout (`d3-force` vs
`FlowSimulation`) on the **same** graph shape. Scene build and drag
are RangerFlow-only in Node — React Flow paints through the DOM.

## 100 nodes / 113 edges

| Step | RangerFlow | React Flow stack | Ranger vs RF | Note |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| edge paths (64000) | 24 ms | 47 ms | 1.99× faster | EdgeRouter vs getBezier/Straight/SmoothStep |
| force layout, 300 ticks | 36 ms | 58 ms | 1.60× faster | FlowSimulation vs d3-force, same graph |
| layered layout | 1.90 ms | — | — | Ranger only — React Flow has no built-in Sugiyama |
| scene build (fit) | 32 ms | — | — | 100 drawn / 0 culled |
| scene build (1:1 zoom) | 10 ms | — | — | 15 drawn / 85 culled |
| drag, ms/frame | 4.18 ms | — | — | EVG display-list rebuild (RF is DOM) |

## How to read this

- **Path and force rows are the fair fight.** Same cases, same graph,
  same machine, Node only.
- **Scene / drag in Node** measure RangerFlow's EVG display-list path.
  React Flow's equivalent is React reconciliation + SVG/HTML nodes.
- Behavioural parity (does the line go the same place?) is scored by
  `npm run rangerflow:parity`, not here. Last checked overall **~98.6%**.
